label: Remnant star cruiser
note: IP-neutral. Issue #193: the Remnant's star cruiser, holding orbit over the home planet far to the east, out of sight of the port but plain to see from space. Its geometry is code (src/systems/world/cruiser_hull.gd, all in the cruiser's own frame: x to starboard, where the bay opens, y up, z bow to stern); where it hangs is the home world's 'cruiser' landmark (content/core/worlds/port_desert.json). This file is everything else: its pads and the ships parked on them, how Z docks you, who is aboard, the droids, the reward and every line. Points are [x, y, z] in the cruiser's frame: the bay, corridor and shaft decks are at y -14, the bridge at 58, its crew pits at 55. When the general is dead the cruiser is taken (WorldState flag cruiser_taken): nobody is aboard from then on, and it is still there to fly to and walk round.

dock.note: Z within radius metres of the cruiser (any altitude, a fight running or not) flies you round the hull, in through the bay's shield at hold_y, turns you round over the dock pad and sets you down, nose out to space. The flight is one smooth curve from where you are, leaving along your heading: up to speed (m/s, accel m/s/s), braking at brake m/s/s out in space and brake_in from approach_x off the mouth in, so she slides through the shield and stops over the pad; then spin_secs to turn round as she sinks to settle metres over the deck, and the normal landing. Z again gives you the stick back. A fight running is not broken off: while you dock, are down in the bay or walk the decks it goes on without you (nobody targets you), and you are back in it when you fly out. The escort's fight ends when the general dies (or every wave is shot down, or you are).

approach.note: Flying to it. The ball curves away under the straight line from the edge of space to the cruiser, so that line dips below the edge: a fight running is not broken off by that while the nose is within cone_deg of the cruiser and you are no more than floor metres under the edge. Within calm_radius of it normal flight is held to the ship's space-fight speed (its 'flight' block: 48 m/s for an interceptor, not 680 at the edge of space), so flying in through the bay's mouth (which takes you out of the fight, not ends it) does not hand you a ship you cannot line up with the bay; full speed again by calm_out. The escort's fight is never broken off by diving: more than floor metres under the edge you are out of it until you climb back. Any fight in the cruiser's sky follows you (Dogfight.arena_follow): both sides come along instead of turning back to where it started.

aboard_shadow_note: While you are aboard, the sun's shadows reach this many metres instead of the time of day's 700-900: a low sun through the bridge windows otherwise lays stair-stepped shadow edges across the floor.

holo.note: The bridge's holo table: the home planet as the cruiser sees it. The ball, the port, every crash site (the world's wreck landmarks) and this cruiser where they really are on it, and the moon in its real direction. Turned to the world (north and east as on the ground), spinning slowly about the planet's up. radius is the ball's size in metres, lift how high its centre floats over the table top; heights over the ball are squeezed by squeeze (0: on the surface, 1: true to scale) so the cruiser's orbit fits over the table; the moon sits at moon_at times the ball's radius, in its true direction.
